_comment_: P4-A: per-seat capacity map. Replaces the legacy single '4 Devin workers' cap with per-provider + per-model caps, a RAM governor, and a metered-seat class so subscription seats are exhausted before paid-per-token ones.
_comment_order: Expiry-first selection order (Nish, 2026-08-22): devin -> cursor -> cline -> free -> minimax (metered). Implemented in seat-lib.sh pick_seat; this file is data only.
_comment_ram_governor: ram_gb_per_worker=0.75 (2026-08-26, fleet-ops#45). The governor is sized on the TYPICAL worker, not the worst case: live worker RSS measured at mean 35 MB, total 0.07 GiB across running workers, so 0.75 leaves 3x headroom for hot working sets while the divide still fits ~10 lanes in ~10 GiB MemAvailable after the 2500 MB launch floor. The 1.28 that was here before 2026-08-26 was the median of completed-unit MemoryPeak (n=14, p95 4.4 GB, max 4.8 GB) - i.e. sized for the worst case, which the comment said was correct until per-worker caps existed. Now they do: MemoryHigh=3G throttles one worker, MemoryMax=6G is the hard stop, TimeoutStartSec=45min kills a wedge, and systemd-oomd kills at 80%/60s. The tail is bounded by the cgroup, not by a pessimistic per-worker budget, so a single 4.8 GB outlier throttles rather than taking the box into swap. Mechanical re-measurement: `bin/ram-measure` (also wired into fleet-heartbeat-tier1 section 13, history at ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-measurement.json, rolling 10 runs). A re-derive of this number is `ram-measure` + a PR; the heartbeat only makes the measurement automatic, it never edits this file. Per-task-weight cap: NOT applied. task_weight() in seat-lib.sh distinguishes heavy vs light packets, but the 4.8 GB outlier was a single failed worker, not a class of task (n=14: median 1.28, p95 4.4, max 4.8 - the tail is one data point). Live heavy workers measure 0.8 GB. Revisit if the rolling ram-measure history ever shows heavy-class p95 sustained > 3 GB.
_comment_cursor_grok: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high: probe-and-exclude. One strike already (spawnSync ETIMEDOUT at 2026-08-25 00:47 IST). Probed twice after the strike and it responds healthy; cap held at 1 to limit blast radius. Raise to 2 if it stays clean for a week.
_comment_minimax: minimax direct (MiniMax-M3) classified as 'metered' per models.json cost field (input $0.30/M, output $1.20/M) even though the model name says 'Yearly Plus' — the cost field is the source of truth and 'Yearly Plus' is just a tier label. Selection order puts it LAST so subscription seats burn down first.
_comment_ollama_rule: ollama cap only covers deepseek-v4-flash:0731 — the DeepSeek-flash-only standing rule bans ollama/kimi-k2.7-code, ollama/deepseek-v4-pro:0813, and ollama/gpt-oss:20b. seat-lib.sh enumerate_seats() emits every model in models.json; the cap map here is the allowlist by being the only entries listed. (Code-level enforcement is a follow-up if the rule is ever loosened.)
_comment_quota_bench: quota_bench_default_s (fleet-ops#90): fallback bench window in seconds used by seat-lib.sh mark_seat_quota_bench when a provider returns a quota/cap 429 whose error text carries NO explicit reset window. cline=604800 (ClinePass weekly cap), devin=900 (devin 15-min message rate limit). A walled seat is benched until the advertised reset window (parsed from the error) or this default, then fail-open after it expires — never charged to the work item.

ollama._hard_cap: Nish 2026-08-26: hard 4, never probe above (like devin)

_comment_cursor: cursor provider cap=1 (2026-08-25): cursor flakes with spawnSync ETIMEDOUT on long-running jobs; short probes are fine. The provider cap holds the fleet to one cursor worker at a time, and the code-level capable-provider whitelist in seat-lib.sh keeps cursor out of the heavy-task rotation. Raise to 2 if cursor stays clean on long jobs for a week.
_comment_devin: devin provider cap=4 (2026-08-25): devin hit its message rate limit at ~01:30 IST tonight. Auto-restart backoff in pi-issue@.service (Restart=on-failure, RestartSteps=3, ~6 min effective retry) handles the recovery, so the cap stays at 4. If rate-limit hits become daily, lower to 3.
_comment_seat_roster: Nish 2026-08-25: ALL seats available everywhere so work never stops. Ten seats probed live and answering: devin, cursor, cline, ollama (Ollama Cloud), minimax, commandcode, openrouter, grok (SuperGrok via grok-cli), zenmux, hetzner. zenmux and hetzner carry FREE lanes as well as credits, and openrouter has free lanes alongside credits - none of them are metered-only, so none is capped 0. Only providers with no working credential stay at 0.
_comment_credits: openrouter and zenmux are class=metered. pick_seat buckets by class, so they sit after free lanes. Do not list them in free_providers_in_order.
_comment_lane_refresh_384: 2026-08-26 live check (fleet-ops#384). Paid flash on OpenRouter+Zenmux: Qwen 3.8 flash does not exist on either catalog. GLM 5.3 flash is $0.075/$0.25 per M on both but is not in Pi's catalog (pi --list-models miss) and has no league score. DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 on OpenRouter is $0.06 in / $0.12 out per M and scores 0.646 on 171 league tasks (fleet2/eval/LEAGUE.md, 2026-08-20) — cheapest of the three that exist, and the only one with quality evidence plus a live Pi slug. Zenmux DS flash is $0.22/$0.66 (3.7x OpenRouter) so zenmux keeps an empty model allowlist. OpenRouter allowlist is the 0731 slug only — not GLM, not Qwen, not ~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest. MiniMax M3 on CommandCode: slug minimax/minimax-m3-free (the -free form, cline-pass prefix precedent) spawned HTTP 200 at 2026-08-26T16:49:19Z with no cost fields; MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 is the metered twin and is NOT allowlisted. OpenCode has no M3 free slug (ModelError); the bare minimax-m3 id returns CreditsError (would bill) so OpenCode stays cap=0.
_comment_grok: grok cap=0 (2026-08-26): SuperGrok's subscription covers the grok.com app and the grok CLI, NOT the x.ai API. pi reaching api.x.ai/v1 with the CLI's own OAuth token returns 403 'You have run out of credits or need a Grok subscription'. pi also has NO registered grok-cli adapter ('No API provider registered for api: grok-cli'), so the CLI route is not reachable from pi either. Raising this cap requires either x.ai API credits (money - Nish only) or a pi custom-provider extension wrapping the grok CLI. Tracked in fleet-ops#41.
